title: The Ten-Thirty Boat
subtitle: Wednesday: A Ferry, a Dying Man, a Union Hall, a Back Room at the Pelican

setting.name: Port Calloway and Gannet Island, Wednesday 29 October 1952
setting.description: The second day of the clock, and the day the case turns from paper to people. In the morning Nora Kessling takes the 10:30 steam ferry Kittiwake from Pier 3 to Gannet Island, to visit Oskar Lindqvist, the Halvorsen Cannery's night watchman, who is dying in the St. Agnes Sanatorium and who, she hopes, will sign a fresh statement before witnesses. Two of Frank Lusk's men are on the same boat. The party, if it knows, is on it too. The island is fog, cows, a ferry café and the nuns' red-brick sanatorium on a bluff. The last boat back is at 7:10. In the evening, back in the city, the hall of Local 9 on the Tin Mile, where Frank Lusk sits under a mural of a strike he betrayed, and the Pelican Club on its pier on the Flats, where at eleven o'clock Lt. Dunleavy meets a quiet man in a grey Chesterfield in the back room, and Gil Maddox drinks too much at the bar. At two in the morning that quiet man hires a launch to Gannet Island.
setting.atmosphere: The ferry: steam, diesel and wet wool, the saloon's coffee urn and rattling cups, gulls following the stern, the city vanishing into grey behind you and the island appearing out of grey ahead. The sanatorium: carbolic, quiet corridors, the cough from every room, a crucifix, rain on tall windows facing the city across the water. Local 9: cigarette smoke, the clatter of a mimeograph, men in caulk boots, a 1934 mural of strikers and mounted police. The Pelican: a seven-piece band, a singer in green, mirrors, smoke, rye, ferry lights through the windows, money pretending not to be. This is the campaign's most emotional day. Lindqvist is the first person who tells the truth all the way through, and he is dying. Let it land.

keyLocations.name: The Kittiwake, Pier 3 to Gannet Island
keyLocations.description: A 1912 steam ferry, white paint gone cream, with a car deck below and a saloon above with benches, a coffee counter and a brass-railed promenade outside. The crossing is fifty minutes. Departures from Pier 3: 7:10, 10:30, 2:15, 5:40; from Gannet Island: 8:40, 12:00, 3:45, and the last boat at 7:10 p.m.
features: The saloon: benches, steamed windows, a coffee counter run by a purser named Gus Haldane who remembers faces
The promenade deck: wet, windy, private, with a rail and a long drop
The car deck: a delivery truck, a farmer's Ford, a black Hudson if Dunleavy's man is following the party
encounters: Nora Kessling, in the saloon with a cardboard folder in her lap, reading the same page over and over
Two of Frank Lusk's men (Union Muscle), Mickey Brannan and a big silent one called Swede Ekberg, who are following Nora and are bad at it
secrets: Nora's folder holds the photostat of the Lindqvist statement (Clue E1) and a fresh typed copy for him to sign, with two blank lines for witnesses. She is going to ask the nuns to witness it. She would rather the party did, if she trusts them.

Lusk's men have orders to 'find out what the girl's carrying and bring it to Frank'. They will not try anything on the boat in front of witnesses. They plan to take it at the island ferry landing on the way back, or in the fog on the sanatorium road.

keyLocations.name: St. Agnes Sanatorium, Gannet Island
keyLocations.description: A red-brick sanatorium for consumptives and the incurable, run by the Sisters of St. Agnes, on a bluff a mile from the ferry landing up a muddy lane. Three storeys, long verandas where patients are wheeled out in blankets when the rain stops, a chapel, a visitors' room. Sister Bernadette Kerrigan, the sister in charge, runs it like a ship.
features: The visitors' book at the front desk, signed by everyone who comes
Room 22 on the second floor, facing the city across the water: Oskar Lindqvist's
The night: one sister on duty per floor, a porter asleep in his chair, a door to the veranda that does not lock
The chapel, where Sister Bernadette will hear anything said to her and repeat nothing
encounters: Sister Bernadette Kerrigan, who protects her patients from visitors and will be won over only by honesty
Oskar Lindqvist, 63, dying of lung cancer, with perhaps a week left
secrets: CLUE C3 (core, automatic for anyone who reads the visitors' book): N. Kessling, every Sunday since 17 August, room 22. On 2 October: a second visitor for room 22, signed only W.S. (Wendell Sloane came once, alone, frightened Lindqvist badly, and left. Lindqvist did not tell Nora.)

CLUE E2 (core, automatic once the party is in the room with Lindqvist and he has decided to talk; Insight or Persuasion DC 12 to get him there, or Nora's presence): his account. Earl Haskin, Vantreight's plant manager, gave him $200 to be off the pier from midnight till two on 9 March 1946, 'so the union men could be caught breaking in, he said, so there'd be pictures'. He went to a tavern. At one the cannery went up. Three days later he went to the DA's office and told a young assistant DA, Mr. Sloane, everything, and a pretty secretary typed it and he signed. Then a big detective, Dunleavy, drove him to the bus station with $1,000 and told him that if he came back he'd be charged with eleven murders. He came back in 1950 because he was dying and wanted to see the water.

If the party and Nora give him the fresh statement, he signs it, and two of them can witness it (or Sister Bernadette and a novice can). This is the most valuable piece of paper in the campaign while he lives: the Ledger will print a living witness's signed statement.

He has one more thing, which he gives only to Nora: Haskin told him the man who would set the fire was 'a torch from Portland, a professional'. Lindqvist never knew a name. (This is NOT Teague. It is a red herring that will make the party think it is, which is fine; Teague was in the army in 1946.)

keyLocations.name: The Hall of Local 9
keyLocations.description: A brick box on Front Street between two canneries, with CANNERY AND WATERFRONT WORKERS LOCAL 9 in gilt on the window and a mural inside of the 1934 strike: men linked arm in arm, mounted police, a burning car, and, at the front, a young Daniel Kessling with his fist up, painted by a WPA artist. Frank Lusk's office is upstairs.
features: The mural: Kessling at the front, Lusk two places behind him
The hiring board and the shape-up list; the hall is full of men waiting for word of the next ship
Lusk's office: a desk, a bottle, a photograph of Lusk with Sloane at a 1950 Labor Day picnic
A memorial board with eleven names from the Halvorsen fire
encounters: Union Muscle at the door (2), and a hall full of men who will not like outsiders leaning on their president
secrets: CLUE B3 (core, automatic if the party tells Lusk they are working for Sloane): he relaxes and says, 'Then you're on the same errand I am. The DA's got me looking for the same thing you are. Find who's got the paper.' He then realises what he has said.

CLUE E4 (core but costly: needs leverage, not a roll; the leverage is E1 or E2 shown to him, or Nora, or the mural): Lusk confesses. In 1947 he was facing a charge for $3,000 missing from the strike fund. Sloane dropped it, and Lusk testified that Danny had talked about burning the cannery. 'He did say it. Everybody said it. We were all saying it, that winter. I just said he meant it.' He has run Local 9 ever since and has done a great deal of good with it. He will sign a statement only if he knows the truth is coming out anyway.
He did not send his men to hurt Nora. He sent them to get the paper. He does not know what they are capable of; he finds out on Thursday.

keyLocations.name: The Pelican Club
keyLocations.description: The city's best nightclub, on its own pier at the edge of the Flats: a long room with a dance floor, a bandstand, a horseshoe bar, mirrors, and windows over the water where the ferries go by lit up like wedding cakes. Upstairs and at the back, the Crow's Nest, a private card room. It belongs, on paper, to a widow in Spokane; in fact it is neutral ground where Larch Hill, the Hall of Justice and the waterfront all drink, and nobody does business on the dance floor.
features: The bandstand: the Les Vardeman Orchestra and a singer (if Rainy Doucette is played, it is her; otherwise a woman called June Ferris who knows Rainy)
The Crow's Nest: a door with a Bouncer, a card table, a back staircase to the service pier
The bar, where Gil Maddox drinks Wednesdays, and talks when he drinks
A cigarette girl, a photographer with a Speed Graphic, a coat-check girl who sees who leaves with whom
encounters: Gil Maddox, drunk at the bar
Lt. Ray Dunleavy and Ansel Teague in the Crow's Nest at 11 p.m.
Two Bouncers and a Mob Lieutenant (Vic Dorrance) at Maddox's elbow
secrets: CLUE F2 (core, automatic if anyone is in a position to see the Crow's Nest door or the back stair between 10:50 and 11:30): Dunleavy goes up; ten minutes later a quiet man in a grey Chesterfield coat and a grey hat goes up by the back stair from the service pier; they talk for twenty minutes; the quiet man leaves the way he came and walks to a cab. The coat-check girl (Insight or Persuasion DC 12, or $5) says he gave no name, 'he tipped a quarter, exactly a quarter, like a man who's read how much you tip'. The club photographer has a picture of the dance floor with the back stair in it (Iris Nakamura can get the negative).

CLUE D4 (core, automatic for a singer or anyone Maddox decides to impress): Maddox, drunk, says 'Wendell's going out with a bang. You read the papers Friday.' He laughs. Dorrance tells him to shut up.

CLUE G2 (core, automatic with Streetwise in the Pelican or anywhere on the Flats, no roll): ask about Elmer Dahl and anyone tells you he's Dunleavy's stoolie; 'Ray gets a call from Elmer every time a gun goes out of that shop'.

Maddox will meet the party if they ask. He wants Sloane to suffer, not to be found to have suffered; he will deny the bomb absolutely and offer the party $1,000 to 'tell the DA there's no hard feelings and he should lose the grand jury report'. Insight DC 15: he is lying about something big, and he is afraid of someone who is not Sloane (Vantreight).

keyLocations.name: Maddox's Boathouse
keyLocations.description: A tarred shed on pilings a hundred yards along the boardwalk from the Harbor Social Club, with a slip for a speedboat and a padlocked loft. It is where Maddox's men keep things they do not keep at the club.
features: A Chris-Craft runabout in the slip
The padlocked loft, reached by a ladder
A Guard Dog chained under the boardwalk
encounters: A Dockside Goon asleep in the speedboat, and the dog
secrets: CLUE D3 (core, automatic for anyone who gets into the loft): the case of DuPont 40% from the viaduct yard, missing eight sticks; a coil of wire; a box of blasting caps; a dry-cell battery; and a sketch on the back of a Harbor Social Club bar tab of a car's underside, the starter motor circled. Breaking in is +2 Heat if anyone sees it.

If the party takes or ruins the dynamite tonight, Maddox simply has Dorrance steal more on Thursday, and the bomb still goes under the Packard, an hour later and with a hasty wire that may not work. The party has made it more dangerous, not less, unless they tell someone.

synopsis: Wednesday is the day the party meets the truth. Nora Kessling goes to Gannet Island on the 10:30 ferry to get the dying watchman, Oskar Lindqvist, to sign a fresh statement. Frank Lusk's men follow her. If the party is on the boat, they can meet Nora properly, see the photostat, and decide whether to protect her or to report her to their client. At St. Agnes Sanatorium, Lindqvist tells the whole story: the $200 to be off his post, the fire, the young assistant DA, the typed statement, the big detective who put him on a bus. He can sign a fresh statement before witnesses. On the road back to the last ferry, Lusk's men try to take the paper. In the evening the party can lean on Frank Lusk at the Local 9 hall (he confesses his perjury, or reveals that Sloane has him hunting the paper too), and at the Pelican Club they can see Lt. Dunleavy meet a quiet professional in a grey coat, and hear Gil Maddox boast that Sloane is going out with a bang. At 2 a.m., having heard from Lusk's men through Sloane where Nora went, Dunleavy sends the professional, Ansel Teague, across the sound by hired launch to make sure Lindqvist never signs anything again. If no one is guarding him, Lindqvist is dead by morning.
hook: Wednesday, 9:50 a.m., Pier 3. The rain has thinned to a cold drizzle and the Kittiwake is getting up steam, gulls on every piling, a queue of farm trucks for the car deck. If the party has found Nora, they know she is going; if not, Ambrose Pell, the morgue's checkout card, or a word from Mrs. Sorvik's sister sends them to the ferry, where a young woman with a cardboard folder is buying a ticket, and two men in union jackets are pretending to read the timetable behind her.

conclusions.conclusion: C. Nora Kessling sent the threat and has a copy of the statement
clues: C3: the St. Agnes visitors' book (Gannet Island)
Her folder on the ferry, E1 (the Kittiwake)
C4: Dahl's ledger, if missed on Tuesday (Water Street)

conclusions.conclusion: E. Vantreight's plant manager paid for the fire and Sloane buried the watchman's statement
clues: A3 from Tuesday: the withdrawn statement initialled W.S. (the archive)

conclusions.conclusion: F. Dunleavy is working with a professional
clues: F2: the Crow's Nest meeting (the Pelican)
Lindqvist: the big detective put him on a bus in 1946 (St. Agnes)
The night launch to Gannet Island (the Flats, 2 a.m., or Thursday morning)

conclusions.conclusion: D. Maddox is planning to bomb Sloane
clues: D1: the dynamite theft (the viaduct yard)
D4: Maddox at the bar (the Pelican)

conclusions.conclusion: G. Nora is being set up
clues: G1: the pencil note in Dahl's ledger (Water Street)
G2: Dahl is Dunleavy's stool pigeon (anyone on the Flats)
Nora herself: the pawnbroker 'recommended' the Colt unasked (the ferry or the island)

acts.title: Act 1: The Kittiwake
acts.description: Wednesday morning. The 10:30 ferry, fifty minutes across the sound. If the party is aboard, this is their chance to talk to Nora properly, somewhere she cannot run. If they are not, they can take the 2:15 and arrive with two hours to spare before the last boat, or hire a launch. Lusk's men are aboard either way.
objectives: Get on the boat Nora is on, or the next one
Talk to Nora and earn enough trust to see what is in her folder
Notice Lusk's men and decide what to do about them
Decide whether to tell Sloane anything tonight

scenes.name: Fifty Minutes
scenes.description: The saloon, the promenade deck, the car deck. Nora sits by a window with her folder. She recognises the party if they came to the Ledger or Mercer Lane. She is frightened of Sloane's people and furious with herself for being frightened. If the party is honest about who hired them and why they have come, she will talk. If they are not, she will stay in public and get off at the island and walk fast.
scenes.readAloud: The Kittiwake shudders and backs out of Pier 3 with a long sad blast of her whistle, and the city goes grey behind her: the viaduct, the canneries, the Courier Building, Larch Hill with its big houses vanishing into cloud. The saloon is warm and full of steam, farmers' wives and a priest and a soldier going home on leave. The young woman from the switchboard is by the window with a cardboard folder on her knees and both hands flat on it, and when she sees you come in, she does not get up. She just closes her eyes for a second, as if she has been expecting you all her life. 'He sent you,' she says. 'Didn't he. Sit down. If you're going to take it, you're going to have to take it in front of all these people.'

skillChecks.success: She believes you are not simply Sloane's dogs. She shows you the photostat (E1): a typed statement dated 12 March 1946, signed Oskar Lindqvist, taken by W. Sloane, Asst. D.A., typed by C. Muir, naming Earl Haskin, plant manager, Halvorsen Packing, and $200. She says it came in the mail in July with no letter. She tells you about Friday: 'I'm going to stand up at his rally and read it out. That's all. Then it's in the paper.' She asks you to witness the new statement.
skillChecks.failure: She tells you to go back to Sloane and tell him she is not afraid of him, which is a lie. She will still let you walk with her to the sanatorium if you keep your distance.

skillChecks.success: When she says 'that's all', she touches her handbag. There is a gun in it. She does not know whether she would use it, and she is more frightened of that than of Sloane. Asked about the gun gently, she says the man in the pawnshop 'was very helpful, he picked it out for me, I'd never have known which'.
skillChecks.failure: She is determined and frightened. You cannot tell what she means to do on Friday.

skillChecks.success: Two men in Local 9 windbreakers at the coffee counter, one small and talkative and one huge and silent, have been watching Nora since Pier 3 and are now watching you. The purser, Gus Haldane, mutters that the small one asked him what time the last boat back was, twice.
skillChecks.failure: You notice Lusk's men only when they get off at the island behind you.

scenes.name: Words at the Rail
scenes.description: An optional confrontation on the promenade deck with Lusk's men, if the party goes out to confront them, or if they come out to have a word with the party. They are union men and not killers; they are on a frightened boss's errand, and the small one, Mickey Brannan, knew Danny Kessling. A fight on the boat is +1 Heat (the purser reports it) and could put someone over the rail.
scenes.readAloud: The promenade deck is wet and the wind off the sound takes the breath out of your mouth. The two men from the coffee counter are at the rail, smoking with their hands cupped. The small one sees you and flicks his cigarette into the wake. 'You're the DA's,' he says. 'So are we, sort of. Ain't that a laugh.'

skillChecks.success: Brannan admits Frank Lusk sent them to 'see what the girl's got and bring it back', and that 'Frank's doing a favour for the DA'. That is a version of B3. He does not want trouble; he says if the party has the paper, then the party has it, and he goes back to the saloon. They will still try at the landing unless the party makes them believe the paper is gone.
skillChecks.failure: Swede Ekberg puts his hand flat on someone's chest and pushes them against the rail, gently, as a warning. The next time is not gentle.

skillChecks.success: Brannan knew Danny Kessling. 'He got me my card in '36.' If the party tells him what the paper is, he goes quiet, and says, 'Frank never told us that,' and he and Ekberg take the 12:00 boat back without trying anything. Lusk learns tonight that his own men will not do this.
skillChecks.failure: Brannan says a man has to eat and goes back inside.

encounters: Mickey Brannan and Swede Ekberg (2 Union Muscle), Lusk's men, on an errand they do not much like
Dunleavy's tail, if not lost on Tuesday (Crooked Cop), on the car deck in the Hudson; he radios nothing from the ferry but telephones Dunleavy from the island café

acts.title: Act 2: Room 22
acts.description: Gannet Island, from late morning to the last boat. The sanatorium, Sister Bernadette, the visitors' book (C3), and Oskar Lindqvist (E2). The emotional centre of the scenario. If Nora is with the party, she does most of the talking; if not, the party must win the old man themselves. The act ends with the walk back to the landing in the fog, where Lusk's men try for the paper.
objectives: Hear Lindqvist's account and, if possible, get it signed before witnesses
Decide what to do with the signed statement: Nora keeps it, the party keeps it, it goes to the Ledger tonight
Get back to the city on the last boat, with the paper, past Lusk's men
Decide whether Lindqvist needs protecting tonight

scenes.name: Sister Bernadette
scenes.description: The front desk of St. Agnes. Sister Bernadette Kerrigan, sixty, Irish-born, ran a field hospital in France in 1918 and is not impressed by anyone. She protects Lindqvist from visitors he does not want. Honesty works; a badge (Cop's The Badge) works, grudgingly; Nora's presence works entirely. The visitors' book is on the desk (C3, automatic).
scenes.readAloud: St. Agnes stands on its bluff in the fog like a red-brick ship, three storeys of tall windows, verandas with patients in wicker chairs wrapped up to their chins, and the sound everywhere, from every open window, of people coughing. Inside it smells of carbolic and floor wax and boiled cabbage, and there is a crucifix over the front desk, and under the crucifix a tall nun in a white wimple is writing in a ledger with a steel pen. She does not look up until she has finished the line. 'You are not family,' she says, 'and you are not from the parish, and you are not the doctor. Which leaves very few reasons for you to be standing on my floor.'

skillChecks.success: She lets you up, and says, as you go, that 'Mr. Lindqvist had one other visitor this autumn, apart from the Kessling girl, a gentleman who signed with his initials and left him weeping, and I would be grateful not to see that again'.
skillChecks.failure: She says Mr. Lindqvist is resting and you may come back on Sunday. Nora, a badge, a long talk in the chapel, or another check after a scene's wait gets you in.

skillChecks.success: The visitors' book (C3) in a minute: N. Kessling every Sunday since 17 August; W.S., 2 October, 3 p.m. to 3:20.
skillChecks.failure: C3 is still found; it just takes Sister Bernadette's disapproving five minutes.

scenes.name: What the Watchman Saw
scenes.description: Room 22. Lindqvist is gaunt, yellow, propped on pillows facing the window and the city across the water. He talks in short breaths with an oxygen mask he lifts to speak. He tells the whole story (E2) if Nora is there, or if the party has been honest and gentle. He wants absolution more than justice. He will sign the fresh statement; it needs two witnesses who are not Nora.
scenes.readAloud: The room is small and white and very clean and the window is the whole of one wall, and through it, across six miles of grey water, you can see Port Calloway: the hills, the viaduct, the cranes, and the black smudge on the waterfront that is Pier 9. The man in the bed is so thin that the blanket hardly rises over him. He has a big ruined Scandinavian face and enormous hands lying on the sheet, and when he sees who is with you he lifts the rubber mask off his mouth and says, in a voice like a door in the wind, 'Two hundred dollars. That's what they paid me. You know what eleven people cost? Two hundred dollars. I worked it out. Eighteen dollars and some cents each.'

skillChecks.success: He tells it all (E2): Haskin, the money, the tavern, the fire, the DA's office, the young assistant DA and the pretty secretary who typed it and gave him a glass of water, and the big detective, Dunleavy, and the bus and the $1,000. And Sloane's visit on 2 October: 'He sat where you're sitting. He asked if I'd told anybody. He said it would be a kindness to the girl if I didn't. I said I'd think about it. I'm thinking about it.'
skillChecks.failure: He tells you about the fire and the money, and stops, coughing, and Sister Bernadette sends you out. Come back in an hour, with Nora if you can; he will finish.

skillChecks.success: Days, not weeks. He is lucid now; by the weekend he may not be. If anyone wants his signature, it must be today. You also notice the veranda door at the end of his corridor does not lock, and that his room is the only one with its own outside stair, for the laundry. Someone who wanted to reach him at night could.

He signs the fresh statement with a shaking pen, and two of you witness it, or Sister Bernadette and a novice do. 'There,' he says. 'Tell Danny's girl I'm sorry. Tell her I'm sorry every day.' The paper is now evidence that Hollis Gage will print.
skillChecks.failure: He wants to sleep on it. He asks you to come back tomorrow. (He will be dead tomorrow unless someone guards him tonight.)

scenes.name: Fog on the Landing Road
scenes.description: Dusk, the mile of muddy lane from St. Agnes to the ferry landing, and the 7:10, the last boat. Lusk's men are waiting at the bend by the creamery with a borrowed farm truck across the road, unless the party talked them out of it on the ferry. They want the folder. They have clubs and one revolver they would rather not use.
scenes.readAloud: The fog has come down so thick that the lane is a grey tunnel with hedges on either side, and you can hear the ferry's bell from the landing a long way off, and cows, and your own feet in the mud. At the bend by the creamery there is a farm truck slewed across the lane with its lights off, and two men stepping out from behind it, and a third behind you whom you did not hear at all. The small one says, 'Just the folder, miss. Nobody needs to get hurt over a folder.'

skillChecks.success: They back off. Brannan says Frank can come and get it himself. They let you pass and catch the boat behind you, sullen.
skillChecks.failure: Fight. They want the folder, not blood; they will run if one of them goes down.

skillChecks.success: Through the hedge and across the field to the landing with the folder, and onto the boat as the gangway comes up. The men are left in the fog.
skillChecks.failure: The hedge is barbed wire under the leaves. You arrive torn, bleeding (1d4) and on time.

encounters: Lusk's men at the creamery bend: 2 Union Muscle and a Street Tough from the island (cousin of Ekberg's), with clubs (1d6 bludgeoning); Brannan has a .38 revolver he does not want to fire. They break and run if one goes down or a gun is drawn on them.
If the party stays on Gannet Island past the last boat: the island café, a room for $2 at the landing boarding house, and the night (see Act 3, The Launch)

acts.title: Act 3: Wednesday Night
acts.description: Back in the city on the 7:10, docking at 8. Three places, and the party cannot be at all of them: Local 9 (B3, E4), the Pelican Club (F2, D4, G2), Maddox's boathouse (D3). At 10 p.m. the call to Sloane. At 11 p.m. the meeting in the Crow's Nest. At 2 a.m. Teague hires a launch at the fuel dock on the Flats and crosses to Gannet Island. If no one is guarding Lindqvist, he is smothered at about 3 a.m.
objectives: Confront Frank Lusk, or decide to leave him for later
See who Dunleavy meets at the Pelican
Find out what Maddox is planning
Decide whether Lindqvist needs a guard tonight, and who goes
Decide what to tell Sloane, and what to give the Ledger

scenes.name: The Mural
scenes.description: Local 9 at 8:30 p.m., a meeting just breaking up, men in caulk boots and windbreakers, smoke, the mural. Lusk is upstairs. If his men failed on the island he is frightened; if they refused, he is ashamed. He gives B3 freely if he thinks the party is on Sloane's side. E4 needs leverage: the statement, Nora, or making him stand in front of the mural and look at it.
scenes.readAloud: The hall is emptying, men shrugging into wet coats under the strike mural, and on the wall above them, twelve feet high, painted in 1937 in blues and reds that have gone dark with smoke, a line of strikers links arms against a charge of mounted police. At the front, fist up, mouth open in a shout, is a young man with a jaw you have seen this morning on the ferry. Two places behind him, a broad young man with his arm through his neighbour's is unmistakably, twenty years younger, Frank Lusk, who is standing at the top of the stairs now, a big bald man in shirtsleeves with a glass in his hand, looking down at you. 'You're the ones from the boat,' he says. 'Come up. I'd rather not do this in front of the mural.'

skillChecks.success: Lusk is not a killer and is terrified of becoming one. Show him the statement or tell him what Lindqvist said, and he sits down at his desk and puts his face in his hands and tells you (E4). Then he says: 'Sloane called me Monday. He said if the paper comes out, I go down with him. He said he'd hired some detectives and I was to find it first.'
skillChecks.failure: Lusk gives you B3 and nothing else, and tells you to get out of his hall. He will break on Thursday if pushed again, or on Friday if he sees Nora in danger.

skillChecks.success: In his own hall, with his own men downstairs, you lean on him and he folds: E4. +1 Heat (leaning on a union president in his hall). The men downstairs will remember your faces.
skillChecks.failure: His men throw you out, not gently. +1 Heat. Nobody on the Tin Mile talks to you on Thursday unless Nora or Becerra vouches for you.

scenes.name: The Crow's Nest
scenes.description: The Pelican Club, 10 p.m. to midnight. The band, the singer, the bar where Maddox drinks (D4), and the door to the Crow's Nest where Dunleavy goes up at 10:50 and a quiet man in a grey Chesterfield joins him at 11 by the back stair (F2). Streetwise anywhere gives G2. A party member who is the band's singer, a waiter, or a guest at the right table sees it all; trying to listen at the door is Stealth DC 16 against the Bouncer and, if it works, gets only a fragment: 'Eight-forty,' and 'the girl'll be in the balcony,' and 'you get the second piece when it's in the paper.'
scenes.readAloud: The Pelican is full and loud and gold, the band playing something slow, couples on the floor, mirrors doubling every lamp, and beyond the long windows the last ferry from the island sliding past lit up like a birthday cake. At the horseshoe bar a heavy man in a beautiful suit is telling the bartender a joke he has told before, and the thin man with the pencil moustache beside him is not laughing. Across the room, a big red-faced man with a toothpick goes through a door by the bandstand that a Bouncer opens for him without being asked. At eleven o'clock exactly, through the window, you see a man come up the service stair from the pier: grey coat, grey hat, a face you would forget while you were still looking at it.

skillChecks.success: You get a good look at the grey man: about forty-five, neat, clean-shaven, a small scar through one eyebrow, gloves he does not take off, a paperback in his coat pocket. He leaves at 11:25 the way he came, and takes a Yellow Cab from the end of the pier. A tail is three successes before three failures (Stealth or Driving against his passive Perception 16). If it works: the Hotel Meridian, where he collects key 914 (sets up F1 for Thursday).
skillChecks.failure: You see a grey coat on the back stair and nothing else. The coat-check girl ($5) remembers the exact quarter.

skillChecks.success: Sung to, or danced with, or flattered, Gil Maddox talks (D4, with detail): 'Wendell's going out with a bang. You read the papers Friday, sweetheart. Six years I paid that man. Six years. And Friday he's going to stand on that viaduct and indict my boys so he looks clean for the hilltop.' Dorrance gets him away from the bar.
skillChecks.failure: Maddox says only 'You read the papers Friday,' and winks. That is D4 in its bare form; it is still a core clue.

scenes.name: The Launch
scenes.description: 2 a.m. on the Flats and 3 a.m. on Gannet Island. Teague hires a launch from a skipper called Hal Ostby at the fuel dock for $40 and a story about a sick aunt, crosses in an hour, walks up the laundry stair at St. Agnes, and smothers Lindqvist with his own pillow. If anyone is guarding the old man (a party member who stayed on the island, Sister Bernadette warned and sitting up, Becerra sent over by the party), Teague sees it from the veranda, withdraws without a fight, and is back at the Meridian by five. If the party ambushes him, he is The Professional and will kill to get away; he does not want to fight at all.
scenes.readAloud: The sanatorium at three in the morning is the quietest place you have ever been: the coughing has stopped, the corridor light is a single bulb, and the rain ticks on the veranda roof. You have been sitting by the old man's door for three hours. Outside, on the laundry stair, a board creaks. Then nothing. Then, through the frosted glass of the veranda door, the outline of a hat, perfectly still, as if the man under it were listening to you breathe.

skillChecks.success: You hear the launch's engine cut out below the bluff at 2:55 and are ready. When the shape appears at the veranda glass you see the grey coat and the scar through the eyebrow, and he sees that you have seen him, and he is gone down the stair before you reach the door. Lindqvist lives. Teague now knows the party's faces.
skillChecks.failure: The shape at the glass is gone before you are sure it was there. Lindqvist lives; you are not certain why.

skillChecks.success: If the party is lying in wait unseen: Teague comes all the way in. You can take him in the corridor; he fights (The Professional) and tries to get back down the stair to the launch. Alive and captured, he says nothing at all, ever, without a deal; dead, he has a Meridian key in his pocket and no papers.
skillChecks.failure: Teague sees a shadow in the wrong place and leaves without coming in.

encounters: Local 9: Frank Lusk and 2 Union Muscle downstairs; nobody fights in the hall unless the party starts it

The Pelican: 2 Bouncers at the Crow's Nest door; Gil Maddox (Waterfront Boss) and Vic Dorrance (Mob Lieutenant) at the bar; Dunleavy (Bent Detective); Teague (The Professional). No fight is expected; a fight in the Pelican is +2 Heat and closes the club to the party.
Maddox's boathouse: a Dockside Goon asleep in the Chris-Craft and a chained Guard Dog. D3 in the loft.

Gannet Island, 3 a.m.: Ansel Teague (The Professional), alone, armed with a .32 pocket pistol and a straight razor and no wish to fight. He breaks off on any sign of a guard. If cornered he fights with everything he has and is the most dangerous person the party has met.

npcsInvolved.name: Nora Kessling, 26
npcsInvolved.role: The sender of the threat; the dead man's daughter; potential companion
npcsInvolved.description: Full sheet in the companion files. On the ferry she is braced for a fight and brave about it; at Lindqvist's bedside she holds the old man's hand and does not cry until afterwards, in the fog, and then not for long. From this scenario on, if the party has earned her trust, she can travel with them.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Friday. Her father's name in the paper, cleared.

npcsInvolved.name: Oskar Lindqvist, 63
npcsInvolved.role: The Halvorsen Cannery night watchman; the living witness
npcsInvolved.description: Huge, gaunt, yellow-skinned, dying, with a ruined handsome face and enormous hands. Born in Gothenburg, came over in 1910, worked the canneries forty years. Has been drunk for most of the last six, and is sober now because they will not let him drink in St. Agnes.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Forgiveness, which he does not expect, and to look at the city while he tells the truth about it.

npcsInvolved.name: Sister Bernadette Kerrigan, 60
npcsInvolved.role: Sister in charge of St. Agnes Sanatorium
npcsInvolved.description: Tall, Irish, flinty; an army nurse in France in 1918. Has seen every kind of liar and prefers the honest kind of sinner.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Her patients' peace, which she will defend against district attorneys, detectives and death, in that order.

npcsInvolved.name: Frank Lusk, 49
npcsInvolved.role: President of Local 9; perjured witness at the Kessling trial
npcsInvolved.description: Big, bald, broken-nosed, in shirtsleeves with a glass in his hand. Has built Local 9 into the strongest union on the waterfront and got more men pensions than anyone in its history. Has also put Danny Kessling in the gas chamber with a lie, and has known it every day since.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To keep what he built, and to stop being afraid. He cannot have both.

npcsInvolved.name: Mickey Brannan, 34, and Swede Ekberg, 40
npcsInvolved.description: Brannan is small, fast-talking and quick-tempered; Ekberg is huge, slow and gentle until he isn't. Union Muscle. Neither of them knows what the paper is, and Brannan owes his union card to Danny Kessling.
npcsInvolved.motivation: A day's pay and not letting Frank down.

npcsInvolved.name: Gil Maddox, 51
npcsInvolved.role: Waterfront boss, the Harbor Social Club; the bomb plot
npcsInvolved.description: A heavy, handsome, sentimental man in a beautiful suit, an ex-longshoreman who now owns the shape-up, the numbers and a piece of every loading dock on the Flats. Use Waterfront Boss. Likes singers, the Irish tenor records, and his mother. Has paid Sloane $500 a month for six years.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Revenge on a man who took his money and is about to sell his lieutenants to the grand jury for a headline.

npcsInvolved.name: Vic Dorrance, 38
npcsInvolved.role: Maddox's lieutenant and bomb man; secretly in Dunleavy's pocket
npcsInvolved.description: Thin, pencil moustache, a demolition engineer from the war, cold and tidy. Use Mob Lieutenant. Dunleavy caught him in 1950 and has owned him ever since; Dorrance reports every Maddox plan to Dunleavy, and Dunleavy to Vantreight.

npcsInvolved.name: Ansel Teague, about 45
npcsInvolved.description: Grey coat, grey hat, clean-shaven, a small white scar through the left eyebrow, gloves always on, a paperback Trollope in his pocket. Registered at the Hotel Meridian as an adjuster for Northwest Casualty Mutual of Portland. Use The Professional. Polite, punctual, utterly without interest in anything but the job and Victorian novels. He has done eleven jobs in seven years in four states and been arrested for none.
npcsInvolved.motivation: The second half of $10,000, payable when the Courier prints that the DA is dead.

npcsInvolved.name: Lt. Ray Dunleavy, 48
npcsInvolved.role: Vantreight's man; Teague's handler in the city
npcsInvolved.description: As in pa-scenario-001. Tonight he is in the Crow's Nest and in a good mood, because the old man on the island is about to stop being a problem.

rewards.money: Nothing from Sloane today. Gil Maddox's offer of $1,000 to 'tell the DA no hard feelings' if the party takes it (and if they do, +1 Heat with the honest cops, and Becerra hears of it). Lusk's men carry about $30. If Teague is caught, his wallet holds $380 and a Meridian key.
items: The photostat of the 1946 Lindqvist statement (Clue E1), Nora's, if she lets the party hold it
Lindqvist's fresh signed and witnessed statement, dated 29 October 1952, if he signed it: the campaign's most valuable document while he lives
A note of the St. Agnes visitors' book: N. Kessling every Sunday; W.S. on 2 October (Clue C3)
The Pelican Club photographer's negative of the dance floor with a grey coat on the back stair (via Iris Nakamura)
A Harbor Social Club bar tab with a car's starter motor sketched on the back (Clue D3), if the party got into the boathouse
Frank Lusk's confession, spoken (Clue E4); he has not signed anything yet

twists: Sloane visited Lindqvist on 2 October, three weeks before the letter. He already knew the watchman was alive and talking to someone. He hired the party to find out who, and the party's report tonight may tell him. If the party tells Sloane they have been to Gannet Island, Sloane tells Dunleavy at once and Teague's launch leaves an hour earlier.

Frank Lusk is working for Sloane, not against him. His men's attack on the landing road is the DA's errand, not the union's. Lusk is the easiest of the conspirators to turn, and once turned he is a witness against Sloane.

Vantreight's man Dunleavy knows where Nora went because Lusk's men reported to Lusk, Lusk reported to Sloane, and Sloane told his security man. Everyone who wants the paper buried is talking to everyone else, which is how a sharp party can trace the chain back to Larch Hill.

Lindqvist's 'torch from Portland' and Teague's Portland cover are a coincidence that the party will seize on. Teague did not set the 1946 fire. Do not correct them until it matters; Teague, if ever asked, says only, 'I was in Italy in 1946, sir, with the 88th Division,' which is true.

If Lindqvist dies tonight, the Ledger will not print the photostat alone against Vantreight, and the case needs the original (Constance) or Lusk's confession. If he lives, the Ledger will print on Saturday, and Vantreight, told by Dunleavy on Thursday morning that the old man is alive and guarded, moves everything up (see pa-scenario-003).
dmTips: This scenario is the heart of the campaign. Give the ferry crossing and Lindqvist's room time. Act 1 is about an hour, Act 2 about ninety minutes, Act 3 an hour and a half. The only likely fights are the landing road (short, nonlethal) and, if the party sets one up, Teague at 3 a.m.

Do not let the party get everywhere on Wednesday night. Local 9, the Pelican and the boathouse are three places, and the island is a fourth. Make them split up or choose, and let the choice matter: whoever is on the island saves Lindqvist; whoever is at the Pelican sees Teague.

Telegraph the danger to Lindqvist fairly: Sister Bernadette's 'gentleman who signed with his initials', the unlocked veranda door, the laundry stair, the Medicine check, the fact that Sloane knows where he is. A party that leaves him alone should have been warned three times.

If the party tells Sloane about the island in the ten o'clock call, he says 'Good work,' in a voice like a man stepping off a kerb, and the clock moves an hour faster tonight. Let them work it out afterwards.

Teague should be terrifying because he does not fight. He comes, he sees a guard, he leaves. If he is cornered, use The Professional's full block and do not soften it; the party is fourth level and he is CR 5. The right move is to let him go and follow him, or to be ready with Becerra and a shotgun.

If the party takes Lindqvist's signed statement straight to Hollis Gage at the Ledger on Wednesday night, Gage will hold it for Saturday's paper, after the lawyers have read it, and put it in his safe. Nora will want to read it aloud on Friday first. That disagreement is good drama.

Period texture: the ferry's coffee is a nickel and tastes of the urn; the Pelican's cover is $2, a rye is 60 cents; a cab across the Flats is 75; the band plays 'You Belong to Me' twice. Radio news: the Ike and Adlai tours, a truce talk at Panmunjom going nowhere.

End the day with two headlines. Courier, Wednesday evening: UNION MEN IN FERRY BRAWL? (only if there was a fight on the boat). Ledger, Thursday morning: if Lindqvist died, GANNET ISLAND PATIENT DIES IN SLEEP on page 14; if he lived and the party told Gage, nothing yet, and Gage's lawyer is reading.

Level-up note: 3,800 XP per character, taking each detective from 4th to 5th level (6,500 XP). Proficiency becomes +3: update attack bonuses. Award it when the party gets off the last boat, or at dawn if they stayed on the island.
